target.title: Simplify cost labels and clarify estimate provenance
target.body: ## Summary Simplify cost navigation labels and move the general cost explanation from the menu into Cost settings. - Rename provider cost buttons and sections to the consistent label `Cost` - Move the general reported-versus-estimated explanation to the bottom of Cost settings - Keep one short Codex-specific note beside its displayed values: `Estimated from token usage · not a subscription bill` - Show that note directly below `Est. total` inside the Codex Cost submenu so submenu-only layouts retain the estimate context - Remove repeated explanations and obsolete localized labels from menu and chart views - Keep the CLI label explicit because CLI output has no surrounding UI context ## Why The previous menu mixed navigation labels with explanations such as “API-equivalent estimate” and “Token-based cost estimate.” This caused three problems: 1. The labels were long and frequently truncated. 2. The same Cost destination had different names depending on the provider. 3. A single estimate-focused label was not accurate for every provider: some costs are provider-reported, while others are calculated from token usage. A button should clearly describe where it leads, so all provider buttons now use the concise label `Cost`. Moving the general explanation out of the menu also lets cost entries with submenus use a standard native menu row instead of a custom multi-line SwiftUI card. This restores consistent menu sizing, highlighting, and interaction behavior. The general explanation applies to the Cost feature as a whole, not to one menu item. It now appears in Cost settings, where users can see that values may be provider-reported or estimated from token usage at public API prices, and that estimates are not subscription charges. Codex keeps a short explanation next to its displayed values because its prominent dollar amounts are token-derived and could otherwise be mistaken for an actual bill. It appears under the inline dashboard details and directly below the estimated total in the Cost submenu, preserving the necessary context without bringing the long explanation back to the parent menu row. The CLI retains `Codex token-based cost` because terminal output must explain itself without relying on the menu or settings UI. ## Result The menu is shorter and more consistent, while the distinction between reported costs, token-derived estimates, and subscription billing remains available where users need it. ## Validation - Focused cost, menu, settings, CLI, and localization tests: 134 passed - Final Codex submenu update: all 28 `CostHistoryChartMenuViewTests` passed - `make check` - `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` - Manually verified the complete change set in the app, including the native Cost row, Cost settings explanation, inline Codex estimate hint, and the Codex submenu note below `Est. total` ## Screenshot before after

target.title: Redesign usage share card around model activity
target.body:
## Status

Ready for product and maintainer review. The attached 1200×630 image is the approved **design target**, not runtime export proof. This PR should not merge until the data contract and renderer dependencies below are resolved, but the proposal is ready for direct review rather than draft-only discussion.

## Direction

- make token volume and dated activity the primary share story
- show a bounded model + source long tail instead of an unbounded provider table
- keep native currencies separate and disclose incomplete pricing
- generate locally without prompts, account identity, paths, projects, or raw events

## Design target

![CodexBar usage share-card concept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/a77e8aafd59c22e016891683799bf7fed3ce085f/docs/screenshots/share-stats-brand-card.png)

This image is a deterministic concept capture used to guide the SwiftUI layout. It is not evidence from `ShareStatsRenderer`.

## Dependencies and related work

- #2292 — reliable non-black PNG rendering; land first
- #2308 / #2287 — preserve trustworthy model rows under partial source history; land and rebase first
- #2257 — model-centric identity and cross-provider aggregation discussion
- #2290 — bounded dashboard/share-artifact contract
- #2291 — Usage & Spend hardening tracker
- #2289 — native macOS sharing remains a separate follow-up

## Release blockers

- Preserve source-instance + raw-model route identity internally before presenting `model / source pairs`; do not collapse distinct versions into a generic family count.
- Use the selected inclusive window bounds for the card date range. Quiet trailing days must not shift a 30-day snapshot backward.
- Represent partial daily-token coverage and invalid/overflow days explicitly; missing data must not render as confirmed zero activity.
- Represent known spend and pricing coverage per native currency without dropping a known subtotal or implying that one displayed currency covers another.
- Count observed, safe-to-display, and hidden model routes separately so the overflow line cannot claim every route is shown after sanitization.
- Keep claims within the accepted cost-history dashboard scope. OpenRouter/OpenCode/Amp routing is not supplied by this pipeline today.
- Replace the concept image with freshly exported SwiftUI evidence from the final renderer at 1200×630, 600×315, and 300×158.
- Add representative runtime fixtures for 1, 4, 8, and 20 sources; partial/unavailable history; mixed currencies; multiple accounts; same model through multiple sources; unsafe labels; and quiet final days.
- Run both macOS CI shards and the aggregate CI gate before merge.

## Current validation

- `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` — 11 passed
- `swift test --filter SpendDashboardModelTests` — 28 passed
- `make check` — passed
- `make test` — 716 selections across 60/60 groups passed
- Linux x64, Linux arm64, Linux musl, lint, and secret checks passed in CI

The earlier draft run deferred macOS tests, which made its aggregate gate red. Marking the PR ready requests the full review and CI path; those checks are required before merge.

target.title: Fix StepFun login web ID
target.body:
## Summary

- derive the StepFun login web ID from the anonymous token before building the Cookie header
- add a regression assertion for the complete password-login Cookie header

## Root cause

The login request interpolated `self.webID`, which is a function reference after `webID(forToken:)` was introduced. Swift emitted a warning and the resulting Cookie header could contain a function debug description instead of the required web ID.

## Impact

Password-based StepFun fallback login now sends a valid `Oasis-Webid` value and the production build no longer emits the function-interpolation warning.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter StepFunTokenRefreshTests` — 8 tests passed
- `swift build -c release` — passed without the StepFun warning
- `make check` — passed

target.title: Fix black PNG exports from usage share cards
target.body:
## Summary

- render usage share cards with SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` instead of an offscreen `NSHostingView.cacheDisplay`
- preserve the exact 1200×630 PNG contract
- strengthen the renderer regression test so a valid-but-uniform black PNG fails

Fixes #2286.
Part of #2291.

## Production evidence

The installed 0.44.0 (build 106) app returned a structurally valid 1200×630 PNG from **Copy Image**, but every pixel was black:

```text
size=1200x630 colors=1 min=0 max=0 mean=0
```

The final renderer tree (`ddd39620`, unchanged by tree-identical CI retry head `d4e836fb`) rendered the same synthetic payload through `ShareStatsRenderer.pngData(for:)` as visible, non-uniform output:

```text
size=1200x630 colors=1032 min=4112 max=65535 mean=21126.8
```

![Synthetic usage share card rendered from the unchanged renderer tree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/ddd39620/docs/screenshots/share-stats-renderer-after.png)

The screenshot uses synthetic fixture data only. It was freshly generated from the final renderer path after the maintainer's no-Metal revision.

## Verification

- `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` — 12 tests passed on the unchanged renderer tree
- `file` / `sips` — RGBA PNG, exactly 1200×630
- ImageMagick pixel inspection — 1,032 colors; non-uniform visible output
- `make check` — passed, including SwiftFormat and SwiftLint
- `make test` — 715/715 selections passed across 60/60 groups, with zero retries and zero timeouts

## CI evidence

`d4e836fb` is an empty, tree-identical retry commit because contributor permissions cannot rerun a failed GitHub job directly.

- exact-head Linux x64 passed the full test and CLI smoke steps: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659631050/job/88119915545
- exact-head Linux arm64 passed: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659631050/job/88119915479

target.title: Serialize flaky Claude CLI platform-gating cases
target.body:
## Summary

- serialize only the two parameterized Claude CLI platform-gating cases
- preserve the per-mode assertion that logged-out `.auto` and `.cli` runs invoke only `auth status --json`
- keep the containment test-only; no production concurrency behavior changes

Fixes #2309.

This flake surfaced in #2292's unrelated Linux x64 shard. Both parameterized cases started together and failed the same invocation assertion even though each already uses UUID-scoped binary and log paths. The deeper shared runtime boundary is not proven, so this PR takes the narrowest safe containment.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter PlatformGatingTests` — 10/10 passed
- `make check` — passed; 0 SwiftFormat changes and 0 SwiftLint violations across 1,572 files
- `make test` — passed all 716 selections in 60/60 groups, no retries or timeouts
- `git diff --check` — passed

Linux x64 CI is the authoritative regression gate for the originally observed flake.

## Exact-head Linux proof

- Linux x64 passed on commit `27230574533f2ee2566dd8f0ed3e1771b304bbef`: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659074330/job/88118445749
- Linux arm64 passed on the same commit: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659074330/job/88118445750

Both jobs retained the full Linux test step and CLI smoke test. The remaining macOS jobs are queued and unchanged by this `TestsLinux`-only diff.
